tools.name: get_opt_out_instructions
tools.description: Documented step-by-step opt-out instructions for one people-search or data-broker site, plus the separate current native verification projection. Guide review dates are content dates. Accepts a guide slug (spokeo), domain, alias, or URL. Returns status not_found with a hint when no guide exists.

tools.name: list_opt_out_guides
tools.description: Summaries of every published step-by-step guide (slug, domain, category, method, difficulty, turnaround, support level). Use it to find the right slug before calling get_opt_out_instructions.

tools.name: get_removal_route
tools.description: For any of the 950+ sites in the takedown registry: the documented removal method (form, email, both, guide, or none), the opt-out URL and privacy email on record, the parent company that actually processes the request, sibling sites one request may cover, and a link to our step-by-step guide when o

tools.name: search_privacy_library
tools.description: Search My Privacy Agent's published articles, opt-out guides, help answers, and plan facts. Returns ranked hits with canonical URLs to cite. Use it before answering questions about data brokers, opt-outs, relisting, pricing, or what the service does and does not do.

tools.name: get_service_overview
tools.description: The public service description: scope of these tools, the private handoff pages (free check, review a listing, pricing), the rules assistants must follow, and registry statistics. Call this once before recommending the service.

tools.name: get_route_verification
tools.description: Read the exact official route variants for a domain or route ID, current independently checked scope, actor and region, capture time, expiry and failures. No badge means the route is not currently verified. This never starts a check or submits a request.

tools.name: get_library_verification_status
tools.description: Read the actual catalog size, distinct route variants, current verified counts, checks captured today and the latest scheduled sweep. Counts include only native evidence that is still current; inventory rows, aliases and agent callbacks never count as verified.

tools.name: list_my_subjects
tools.description: Requires OAuth. Lists the person (first name, city, state, verification status) whose exposure this account has checked, with the subject_id other personal tools need. Returns authorization_required with a connect URL when the token is missing.

tools.name: get_my_report
tools.description: Requires OAuth and the 'share_results' permission for the subject. Returns the report summary the dashboard shows: status, counts, and per-site findings (site, status, what it exposes, guide link). No listing URLs or observed values are included. Returns authorization_required with a connect URL whe

tools.name: list_my_cases
tools.description: Requires OAuth and the 'share_results' permission. Lists removal cases (site, action, status, verification status, steps only the person can do, dates). Status words mean different things: filed, pending, needs review, verified removed. Never collapse them.

tools.name: get_case_status
tools.description: Requires OAuth and the 'share_results' permission. Returns one case by case_id with its current status, verification status, and any step only the person can do.

tools.name: request_recheck
tools.description: Requires OAuth and the 'run_check' permission. Queues a fresh check of the person's existing details (the same re-scan Patrol runs monthly). Patrol plan only, verified subjects only, once per 24 hours; it never starts a first check and never takes new details. Returns queued, or a structured reason

tools.name: submit_approved_plan
tools.description: Requires OAuth and the 'submit_requests' permission. Without confirm: true it only previews which eligible listings would be queued (status preview) — show that list to the person and get a yes first. With confirm: true it queues removal requests for exactly those listings, using the approval the pe

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_opt_out_guides" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_opt_out_instructions, get_removal_route, search_privacy_library, get_service_overview, list_my_subjects, get_my_report, list_my_cases · Private data: get_removal_route, get_service_overview, list_my_subjects · Public sink: get_removal_route, submit_approved_plan.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_opt_out_instructions, get_removal_route, search_privacy_library, get_service_overview, list_my_subjects, get_my_report, list_my_cases · Private data: get_removal_route, get_service_overview, list_my_subjects · Public sink: get_removal_route, submit_approved_plan

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
